segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Years before, Joseph's own brothers had sold him into slavery out of jealousy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now he was second only to Pharaoh in all Egypt.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the brothers came begging for food in the famine, they didn't recognize the brother they'd betrayed. Then he sent every Egyptian out of the room, and told them.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He didn't soften it and he didn't skip it — he said the worst thing they ever did straight to their faces, and then he kept talking.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Don't tear yourselves up over it, he said. Don't be angry at yourselves that you sold me here. God sent me ahead of you — to keep people alive. He gave them the one thing they could not give themselves: permission to stop hating themselves.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Much later, when their father died and the brothers feared revenge, Joseph spoke the line that closes the wound.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You meant it for evil, he told them — I'm not going to call it anything else. a whole lot of people are still alive. He didn't pretend it hadn't hurt. He saw God's hand turning their evil into rescue.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What others meant for harm, God can mean for good. Let it go.
